items.title: AI: the biggest economic bet in US history
items.content: The US economy continues to expand faster than other G7 economies, but the driver is the humungous investment in AI models, data centres and all the AI-related chips and technology.  The US composite PMI (economic activity measure) rose to 58.4 fom 56 in August, the strongest expansion in private-sector activity since July 2021 and markingContinue reading "AI: the biggest economic bet in US history"

items.title: Russian elections: stagnant politics and economy, unending war
items.content: Russia has elections to its parliament (Duma) starting today. This will also be the first legislative election in Russia to take place amid the ongoing war in Ukraine. At stake are 450 seats in the lower house of the Federal Assembly. Half of the seats (225) are elected by party-list proportional representation with a 5% electoral threshold in number of votes. The otherContinue reading "Russian elections: stagnant politics and economy, unending war"

items.title: Is economics changing?
items.content: In an article entitled How economics is changing, FT columnist Harvey Nripia paints a generally positive picture of economics as an academic discipline in the 21st century.  He argues that economics has become more inventive and empirical and now provides, on the whole, increasingly useful advances in our knowledge about economies and how human societiesContinue reading "Is economics changing?"
